alex: quick question — I need to inspect a single user row in prod (user_id=87) to debug a payment mismatch. Is it okay to run a SELECT on the primary? Trying to confirm safe steps before I touch prod.

oncall-bot: Reminder: all interactive prod sessions are recorded and audited. Refer to runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/prod-access — request approval if you need shell/psql.

maria: short answer: yes, but please follow the runbook checklist. TL:DR: request ephemeral DB role, get SRE approval (ticket id), run read-only queries, and NEVER paste raw PII back into channels. :warning:

maria: if possible, run against a read replica. If you must run on primary, use a read-only role and redact sensitive columns in your query results. Example we use: 
```sql
SET ROLE readonly_user;
SELECT id, encode(digest(email, 'sha256'), 'hex') AS email_hash, substr(phone,1,4) AS phone_prefix, created_at
FROM users WHERE id = 87;
```

samir: also add the approval ticket number to the audit metadata so the security team can correlate. Don't use `pg_dump` or `\copy` — those will materialize full rows into files. If you need a larger export, open a data-ops request and we will provide a scrubbed dataset.

jess: small etiquette notes: 1) open the approval ticket in #infra-approvals and tag @sre-oncall, 2) record the commands you ran in the ticket (no raw output pasted), 3) if you capture any personally-identifiable info accidentally, DM SRE immediately — we have a redaction flow. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks — I'll open an approval now. Ticket created: INFRA-1242. Planning to run the `SET ROLE` + SELECT above on the replica first, then escalate if needed. Will not paste outputs here.

oncall-bot: Note: session start logged at 2026-09-30T14:11:30Z. Audit link: https://redwood-internal/audit/INFRA-1242. :lock:

maria: one extra tip — when you capture query text in the ticket, redact the exact email addresses (replace with `<redacted_email>`). The security team prefers hashes or prefixes only.

alex: got it, thanks everyone. pinging @sre-oncall once I have the replica run done. :thumbsup:
